findings.title: Async legacy writes are derived from the request context and may be cancelled
findings.body: The legacy goroutines in Create, Delete, Update and DeleteCollection build their timeout context from the caller's `ctx`. That context belongs to the incoming API request and is cancelled as soon as the response is returned. The 'fire-and-forget' legacy write can therefore be aborted almost immediately after the unified-storage write succeeds, leaving the legacy store silently out of sync. The legacy write should run on a context detached from the request, for example `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` plus the timeout.

findings.title: Object shared with an asynchronous goroutine while storage may still mutate it
findings.body: In Create, `obj` is passed to `d.Legacy.Create` inside a goroutine while the same object was already handed to `d.Storage.Create`. The storage layer may set fields such as name, UID or resourceVersion on it, and the caller may keep using it after returning. This is a data race on a shared runtime.Object. The legacy write should receive a deep copy.

findings.title: Legacy Update reuses objInfo that was already consumed by the storage update
findings.body: `objInfo` is passed unchanged to both `d.Storage.Update` and the asynchronous `d.Legacy.Update`. The UpdatedObjectInfo's UpdatedObject is typically applied to the current old object. Calling it a second time from another goroutine, against the legacy store's view of the object, can produce a different result from what unified storage stored (or fail), and the two stores can diverge. The legacy write should use the object that storage actually persisted, as the previous implementation did with updateWrapper, and not re-run the mutation.

findings.title: Storage failure in Create is recorded as a legacy failure metric
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the error is recorded with `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`, so unified-storage errors are counted against the legacy store. The same mistake appears in Update (line 129). This corrupts the metrics used to compare the two stores.

findings.title: DeleteCollection legacy timing is recorded with the storage metric
findings.body: The DeleteCollection goroutine reports its outcome via `d.recordStorageDuration` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy delete-collection failures and durations are therefore counted as storage metrics, and the legacy metric stays empty.

findings.title: Delete success metric is labelled with the object name instead of the kind
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes `name` in the kind label position. Every other call passes `options.Kind`. Using the object name gives unbounded label cardinality and breaks the per-kind metric series.

findings.title: Delete attaches the base logger to the context instead of the request-scoped logger
findings.body: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` ignores the `log` value built just above with name/kind/method. Every other method attaches `log`, so Delete logs lose their contextual fields downstream.

findings.title: Legacy delete of an object missing from legacy is reported as a failure
findings.body: The previous implementation ignored NotFound errors from the legacy delete. The new goroutine treats any error as a legacy failure and logs or records it. Objects that were created only in unified storage will now generate spurious legacy errors and failure metrics on every delete.

findings.title: Destroy calls Legacy.Destroy without a nil check and while async writes may still run
findings.body: Destroy tears down both stores immediately, while fire-and-forget legacy goroutines may still be running against Legacy. Calling Destroy can race with those in-flight writes. There is no tracking (WaitGroup or similar) of pending async writes.

findings.title: Tests cannot observe the asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: The mode 3 tests register `Legacy` mock expectations (Create, Update) but never wait for or assert the goroutine calls. The legacy path is never verified, and the mock may be invoked after the test has finished. The tests therefore pass even if the legacy write is never made, cancelled, or made with the wrong object.

findings.title: Test case name says 'not implemented' but List is implemented
findings.body: The case 'error when listing an object in the unified store is not implemented' tests a real List error path, so the name is misleading. The List behaviour itself (reads only from unified storage) is not asserted against the legacy mock either.

findings.title: Unrelated dependency checksums added to go.work.sum
findings.body: The go.work.sum changes add checksums for unrelated modules (grafana-azure-sdk-go, prometheus-alertmanager, otel exporters and others) that this mode 3 change does not touch. This suggests an unrelated dependency resolution leaked into the PR and should be explained or dropped.
